title: goal
description: What an evaluation is FOR: who uses the output, the decision it informs, the measure that decides, and the data that stands for the use. One file per goal, data/goals/<goal_id>.yaml. Runs and baselines name it with `goal:`. Projects may add fields; these are the ones the harness reads.

goal_id.description: Permanent; equals the file name. A materially different purpose is a new goal.

statement.description: One sentence: X for Y so that Z.

decision.description: The decision an answer to this goal informs.

output_contract.description: Every output shape the goal accepts. A run that declares a `format` must match one.

measure.description: The per-item metric that decides, as runs record it.

direction.description: higher or lower ranks the arms; non_inferior is a guard (no significant drop against a baseline) and ranks nothing.

axes.description: What the goal weighs beside quality (ADR-0006). cost (cost_usd, tokens beside it) and speed (latency_ms on its p95) are built in and need no entry; an entry adds a limit, a role or another measure. Any other name is the project's own axis: a per-item metric its runs record. `quality` takes a limit only.

measure.description: The per-item metric, as runs record it. Built-ins default to cost_usd and latency_ms; a project axis defaults to its own name.

direction.description: Which way is better; a project axis defaults to the adapter's METRIC_DIRECTIONS, else higher.

stat.description: What a limit and the tie-break read: speed defaults to p95, everything else to mean.

limit.description: An arm past it is out, with the reason (lower: above it; higher: below it).

margin.description: quality only: how far below the leader an arm the paired test does not separate may be and still count as tied (default: 2% of the leader's mean).

role.description: ignore: the goal does not weigh it (an overnight batch: speed).

note.description: What a reader needs to know about the axis, in words.

strategy.description: How the axes become a recommendation (ADR-0006): who counts as tied with the quality leader. balanced (default): not separated AND within the quality margin; quality_first: the same quality only; frugal: anything the paired test cannot separate.

tie_break.description: Among arms tied on quality, the axes that pick, in order (default: cost, then speed).

guardrails.description: Rules in words that no number checks (a deployment constraint, a gate run elsewhere): shown on the goal page with their source.

min_items.description: The fewest shared items a winner-picking comparison may rest on.

datasets.description: The data that stands for the use. Empty for a goal checked by a gate rather than measured on a dataset.

role.description: dev, heldout, smoke, generalization (a check that never decides), ...
